# Security Checklist: Generic Product-Line Seeder

**Purpose**: Validate security requirement quality for the Generic Product-Line Seeder before task generation.
**Created**: 2026-05-22
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This checklist is generated by the `/speckit.checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.

## Evidence Redaction And Secret Safety

- [x] CHK001 Are redaction requirements complete for structured failure and residue evidence, including an explicit prohibition on credentials, tokens, passwords, raw secret values, signed URLs, raw logs, raw untrusted payloads, and matched secret substrings? [Completeness, Spec §FR-016]
- [x] CHK002 Are `--operator-evidence` input and any echoed or derived operator evidence outputs required to follow the same redaction, hashing, and raw-payload exclusion rules as residue evidence? [Resolved] [Spec §FR-003, §FR-016, §FR-017, Contract §Operator Evidence Redaction]
- [x] CHK003 Are snapshot and hash requirements clear that secret material and raw untrusted payloads are neither emitted nor hashed into review evidence? [Clarity, Spec §FR-017]
- [x] CHK004 Are security failure results required to remain structured and redacted even for unexpected boundary errors? [Completeness, Spec §FR-015, Contracts §Validation Error Codes]

## Safe Config Parsing And Validation

- [x] CHK005 Are YAML parsing requirements explicit that config loading uses a non-executing schema/profile and rejects custom tags, aliases, merge keys, multi-document streams, executable constructs, and remote reference loading before semantic validation? [Resolved] [Spec §FR-005, §SC-006, Contracts §Product-Line Seed Config, Contracts §Validation Error Codes]
- [x] CHK006 Are config identity, version, required sections, duplicate declarations, unknown fields, unsupported fields, and field types validated before write-capable runs can mutate target state? [Completeness, Spec §FR-005]
- [x] CHK007 Are GitHub owner, repository, and full-name requirements validated before writes with target-conflict handling for declared product-line or repository boundaries? [Coverage, Spec §FR-006]
- [x] CHK008 Are feature-flag enabled and disabled/absent inputs validated against the registry, reserved future flag allowlist, duplicate/conflict rules, cascades, and env force-off blockers before writes? [Coverage, Spec §FR-008, §FR-009, §FR-010]

## Side-Effect And Future Activation Boundaries

- [x] CHK009 Are no-GitHub-mutation, no-task-creation, no-dispatch, no-claim, no-runner, no-sandbox, no-harness-adapter, no-auto-merge, and no-SpecKit-setup/autopilot boundaries stated as seeding requirements rather than only implementation assumptions? [Consistency, Spec §FR-026]
- [x] CHK010 Are reserved future runner/sandbox flags required to remain validation-only negative assertions that the seeder cannot write, register, enable, or implement? [Completeness, Spec §FR-009]
- [x] CHK011 Are safety-policy blocked side effects required to include future runtime activation surfaces so future config edits cannot silently authorize runners, sandboxes, harness adapters, auto-merge, dispatch, claims, or GitHub mutation? [Coverage, Spec §FR-001, Spec §FR-026, Contracts §Product-Line Seed Config]
- [x] CHK012 Are Product Line B exclusion requirements explicit enough to prevent seed config, smoke evidence, live target enablement, GitHub mutation, or runtime activation from entering SPEC-010A? [Scope, Spec §FR-025, §SC-012]

## No-Mutation And Existing Target Protection

- [x] CHK013 Are fail-closed requirements clear that incomplete, invalid, unsafe, or target-conflicting configs stop before opening a write transaction? [Clarity, Spec §FR-014]
- [x] CHK014 Are existing-target and residue-blocking requirements detection-only, preserving operator cleanup authority without automatic deletion or unlinking? [Consistency, Spec §FR-018, §FR-027]
- [x] CHK015 Are verify-mode requirements explicitly read-only for both matching and drifted target states? [Completeness, Spec §FR-021, §SC-010]
- [x] CHK016 Are no-mutation proof requirements measurable for invalid-config and blocked-preflight security failures across config-owned and preserved operational surfaces? [Measurability, Spec §FR-017, §SC-006, §SC-007]

## Notes

- Initial checklist generation found two security requirement gaps in CHK002 and CHK005.
- Remediation loop 1 updated `spec.md`, `contracts/cli-result-envelope.md`, `contracts/product-line-seed-config.md`, and `contracts/validation-error-codes.md` so operator evidence is treated as untrusted redacted input and YAML config loading is non-executing, single-document, and remote-reference-free before semantic validation.

- [x] CHK017 Do remediated operator-evidence requirements now classify `--operator-evidence` as untrusted input and prohibit raw echoing, logging, snapshotting, or hashing while preserving actionable redacted evidence? [Completeness, Spec §FR-003, §FR-016, §FR-017, Contracts §Operator Evidence Redaction]
- [x] CHK018 Do remediated YAML parsing requirements now require a single-document non-executing parser profile and reject custom tags, anchors, aliases, merge keys, multi-document streams, executable constructs, constructor/object instantiation syntax, and remote reference loading before writes? [Completeness, Spec §FR-005, §SC-006, Contracts §Product-Line Seed Config, Contracts §Validation Error Codes]
- [x] CHK019 Are the security checklist focus areas still satisfied for GitHub ownership validation, feature-flag validation, reserved runner/sandbox flags, and blocked runner/sandbox/auto-merge side effects after remediation? [Consistency, Spec §FR-006, §FR-008, §FR-009, §FR-010, §FR-026]
